questions.question: In the energy flow diagram of an ecosystem, the flow of energy comes to herbivores from:
questions.questionHtml: In the energy flow diagram of an ecosystem, the flow of energy comes to herbivores from:
questions.solution:
In an energy flow diagram of an ecosystem, energy flows from the sun to producers (plants) to primary consumers (herbivores).


Here's how energy flows through an ecosystem:

Sun

Plants absorb light energy from the sun to produce food for themselves.

Plants

Green plants convert solar energy into chemical energy in food. Some energy is stored in the plants, while the rest is used by the plants.

Herbivores

Herbivores eat the plants, transferring the stored energy to the herbivores. Herbivores use some of the energy for their activities and store the rest in their bodies.

Carnivores

Carnivores eat the herbivores, transferring the stored energy to the carnivores.


Energy flow is the transfer of energy from one trophic level to another. Only 10% of energy transfers from one trophic level to another. This means that the number of trophic levels is limited to only 4 or 5.

questions.solution:
A transfer payment is a one-way payment to a person or organization that does not involve the exchange of goods or services.


In macroeconomics and finance, transfer payments are a way for governments to redistribute income and wealth. They are considered non-exhaustive because they don't directly create output or absorb resources.


Governments and governmental agencies typically make these payments to people who have a poor quality of life and no other means of income. The goal is to improve the lives of individuals without expecting profits.


Examples of transfer payments include: Pensions, Scholarships, Unemployment allowances, Foreign aid.

questions.question: Which of the following statements are INCORRECT? 1) The Original Jurisdiction establishes the Supreme Court as an umpire in all disputes regarding federal matters. 2) The Supreme Court can give special orders in the form of writs. 3) Article 129 of the Indian Constitution mention about appointment of acting Chief Justice of India. 4) Every Judge of the Supreme Court of India shall be appointed by the Prime Minister of India.
questions.questionHtml:

1) The Original Jurisdiction establishes the Supreme Court as an umpire in all disputes regarding federal matters.
2) The Supreme Court can give special orders in the form of writs.
3) Article 129 of the Indian Constitution mention about appointment of acting Chief Justice of India.
4) Every Judge of the Supreme Court of India shall be appointed by the Prime Minister of India.
questions.solution:
The original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court are the cases that can be directly considered by the Supreme Court without going to the lower courts. This establishes the Supreme Court of India as an umpire in all disputes regarding federal matters.


The Supreme Court or the High Court can issue five different types of writs/orders to enforce the fundamental rights of Indian citizens. They are called Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Quo-Warranto, Prohibition, and Certiorari.


Article 129 of the Indian Constitution gives the Supreme Court the power to act as a court of record. This means the Supreme Court has all the powers of a court of record, including the power to punish itself for contempt.


The President of India appoints the judges of the Supreme Court and the Chief Justice of India. The President makes these appointments based on the advice of the Union Law Minister to the Prime Minister. The President also consults with judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts before making appointments.

questions.solution:
The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) is responsible for setting the maximum residue limits (MRLs) of pesticides in food materials. The FSSAI is part of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and is authorized to set limits for the use of food additives, crop contaminants, and other substances.

Most runs in a Test cricket over

First batter to score 31 batting at 10
